title: Kestrel and the Monsoon
premise: Ivo Crane, a riverboat captain who has spent a lifetime outrunning a family name tied to the drowned nation of Vessia, salvages a sealed chest from a shifting sandbar and finds inside it proof that their father was not a smuggler but the last custodian of Vessia's exiled archive. The chest makes Ivo a target for the Meridian Compact, a syndicate of collectors who erase small nations by buying their pasts, and for Sefa, an archivist's daughter who believes the chest belongs to her people. Hunted upriver and then overland, Ivo and Sefa must cross the Karst Range ahead of the snows, through a glacier pass that opens only during calving season. In the pass, Ivo chooses to stop running: they surrender the chest to no one, instead triggering the calving that buries the Compact's expedition and scatters the archive among the villages on both sides of the range — belonging, at last, to everyone who remembers.
about_author: Isandro Kavanagh is a former barge surveyor who spent eleven years charting seasonal waterways across three continents before turning to fiction. He writes adventure novels about people whose homes are vehicles, drawing on his notebooks of river pilots, mountain porters, and the maps they refuse to sell.

chapters.title: The Sandbar That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Running the low-water season on the Serein River, Ivo grounds the kestrel-boat on a sandbar that appears on no chart, and the river gives up a lead-lined chest stamped with the seal of Vessia, a nation erased from every map Ivo has ever owned. The beat is unease: the river knows something about them.

chapters.title: What the Chest Weighs
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Alone in the hold at night, Ivo pries the chest open and finds wax-sealed folios, a brass astrolabe, and a letter addressed to 'the Custodian' — their father's name. They burn nothing and tell no one, but the beat is dread: inheritance arriving like a debt collector.

chapters.title: The Passenger at Kilometer Forty
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. A young woman with a forged transit pass begs passage upriver, paying in old Vessian coin she shouldn't have. Sefa watches Ivo lie smoothly about cargo and recognizes a fellow keeper of false papers. The beat is wary kinship between two liars.

chapters.title: Men Who Buy Rivers
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. At the toll-lock of Harrow Bend, a courteous man named Aldous Vane of the Meridian Compact offers Ivo triple freight rates for 'salvage consulting' and mentions the chest by its registry number. Ivo declines too quickly. The beat is the moment invisibility ends.

chapters.title: Sefa Opens the Letter
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Caught reading the folios in the hold, Sefa reveals she is the daughter of the Vessian archivist who entrusted the chest to Ivo's father; her coin was minted by her grandmother. She reads the custodian's letter aloud. The beat is grief shared before trust exists.

chapters.title: Night Run Through the Reeds
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Compact launches with quiet engines sweep the back-channels; Ivo runs the boat dark through reed shallows only they know, Sefa poling the stern. They escape, but the boat takes a gashed hull. The beat is exhilaration curdling into the knowledge that there is no downriver left to hide in.

chapters.title: The Shipwright of Ossory Quay
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Hauled out for repairs, the boat becomes a beacon; Sefa trades her grandmother's coin to a shipwright who owes Ivo's father a favor, learning that the elder Crane once carried Vessian boxes over the Karst Range every summer. The beat is the first map of the road ahead — and of what Ivo has been refusing to remember.

chapters.title: Everything Ivo Sold
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. In a quay-side tavern, Ivo confesses to Sefa: as a teenager they sold their father's route-notes to a broker to buy their first boat, which is how the Compact learned the pass existed. The beat is shame met head-on; Sefa does not forgive, but she stays.

chapters.title: The Broker's Ledger
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Following the sold notes' paper trail, Sefa breaks into the broker's office and finds the Compact's acquisition ledger: entire nations listed like cargoes, Vessia marked 'pending final delivery.' The beat is cold fury replacing grief.

chapters.title: Vane Makes an Offer
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Vane corners Ivo at the fuel dock: he doesn't want the chest destroyed, he wants it delivered — and he offers Ivo the one thing money can't usually buy, expunged records, a clean name, permission to stop running. The beat is temptation with a human face.

chapters.title: The Name on the Boat Papers
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Reading the offer's fine print, Ivo sees the price: the Compact registers the archive under its own seal, and Ivo's name goes on the transfer as heir-consent — the erasure completed with a Crane signature. They tear the contract. The beat is refusal as identity.

chapters.title: Upriver, Against the Freight
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Loaded with deck cargo as cover, they run upriver toward the Karst foothills while Compact agents buy every lockmaster behind them. Sefa learns the river's grammar from Ivo. The beat is growing partnership, two skills becoming one craft.

chapters.title: The Lockmaster's Daughter
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. At Tern Lock, the lockmaster's daughter hides the boat inside her own barge's lockage to slip it past inspection — because Ivo's father once ran medicine upstream for her village in a famine year. The beat is the discovery that the father's kindness built a hidden network Ivo can still walk through.

chapters.title: What the Villages Kept
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Moored at a hill-stream confluence, they find Vessian words surviving in the villagers' boat-songs, harvest rites, river-names. Sefa weeps at hearing her language alive in strangers' mouths. The beat is belonging discovered where memory was never catalogued.

chapters.title: The Informer
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. A friendly pilot who shared their fire reports their position to the Compact for his son's medical debt; Ivo catches him at it and lets him go with a warning instead of violence. The beat is mercy as strategy — and loneliness, since even kindness now has witnesses.

chapters.title: End of Water
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The river shallows into braids and dies against the foothills; they sell the kestrel-boat to the lockmaster's daughter, who promises to keep her name. Ivo touches the wheel a long time before letting go. The beat is mourning a home that was also a hiding place.

chapters.title: The Porters of Last Light
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. In the trail-town of Last Light, they hire porters for the Karst crossing and discover every guide refuses the high route: the glacier pass opens only during calving season, three weeks away, and the snows are early this year. The beat is the clock starting.

chapters.title: The Old Route-Notes
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Among the chest's folios, Sefa deciphers the father's hand-drawn pass charts — including a branch tunnel beneath the ice the Compact's maps don't show. The beat is hope with teeth: the inheritance is literally a way through.

chapters.title: Vane Buys the Town
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Vane's expedition arrives at Last Light, buying every mule, every bed, every silence; the town that sheltered Ivo starts looking away in the street. The beat is the cost of being known — attention as a kind of exile.

chapters.title: The Mule-Woman of the High Pasture
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. An elderly porter, Dalla, agrees to take them up the forbidden high pasture because she recognizes the astrolabe: her mother engraved it. The beat is an alliance older than either traveler, inheritance passing sideways as well as down.

chapters.title: Above the Tree Line
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Three days climbing, storms chasing them; Ivo's river instincts fail on ice and Dalla teaches them mountain craft — read the snow like water, she says. The beat is humility, the captain becoming a passenger on land.

chapters.title: The Frozen Chapel
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Sheltering in a half-buried waystation chapel carved with Vessian stars, they find pilgrim graffiti centuries deep — the nation didn't die, it climbed. Sefa adds her name to the wall. The beat is continuity, the smallest possible act of defiance.

chapters.title: Avalanche Country
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. A slope lets go above them; Dalla's quick call saves the line but costs their lead mule and half the food. Ivo realizes the Compact party is a day behind and gaining. The beat is fear sharpened into arithmetic.

chapters.title: The Pass That Opens
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. At dawn the glacier begins to calve — thunderous, scheduled, alive — and the ice-tongue route opens exactly as the father's charts promised, for a window measured in days. The beat is awe: the landscape itself keeping Vessia's calendar.

chapters.title: Into the Blue Ice
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. They enter the pass proper, walls of compressed blue ice arching overhead, meltwater roaring beneath. Ivo navigates by the route-notes and, for the first time, feels their father walking beside them rather than judging. The beat is reconciliation with the dead.

chapters.title: The Branch Tunnel
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The charts' secret branch leads to a chamber where the father cached a second cache: letters, photographs, a complete register of every family the archive belongs to. The beat is revelation — the chest was never treasure, it was a mailbag undelivered.

chapters.title: Vane Enters the Ice
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. From a ridge eyelet, Ivo watches the Compact expedition string into the pass below, roped and confident, Vane's red parka unmistakable. The beat is the hunter arrived, and nowhere left to be invisible.

chapters.title: The Choice at the Crevasse Field
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Split by a widening crevasse, Sefa carries the register while Ivo carries the chest; they argue about whether to destroy the archive rather than let it be bought. Sefa refuses destruction — memory isn't hers to kill. The beat is the book's moral hinge.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. A whiteout swallows the pass; the group ropes together and navigates by Dalla's counting-steps and Ivo's feel for current, treating wind like water. The beat is trust made physical — each life literally held on another's rope.

chapters.title: Dalla's Story
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Storm-bound in a snow cave, Dalla tells how the Compact bought her valley's name off the maps when she was a girl, and how her mother engraved astrolabes so children would know where they were from. The beat is the theme stated in a human voice.

chapters.title: The Calving Begins
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. The glacier enters peak calving; seracs collapse around the route, and the Compact party is caught in the open ice below. Ivo could signal them to safety or stay silent. The beat is the cruelest choice in the book, and Ivo fires a flare toward the icefall.

chapters.title: Rescue on the Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. Hauling two stranded Compact porters onto stable ice, Sefa discovers they are conscripted locals, not believers — Vane's empire runs on hired hands from erased places too. The beat is enemies revealed as neighbors.

chapters.title: Vane at Gunpoint of the Glacier
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Vane, separated from his team, confronts them at the branch chamber with a pistol and a lawyer's calm: give me the chest and your record burns tonight. Ivo answers with the register — 'you can't buy what already belongs to everyone.' The beat is confrontation without a shot fired.

chapters.title: The Ice Gives Way
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The chamber floor calves; Vane falls into a crevasse and Ivo goes down the rope after him, hauling him out at cost of the astrolabe, which drops into the blue dark. The beat is Ivo saving the man who offered to unmake them — grace as the final refusal.

chapters.title: Descent Before the Snows
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. With the window closing, they race the calving season down the far side, Compact porters carrying loads alongside them by unspoken truce, Vane limping in custody of his own rescued men. The beat is a strange procession — adversaries fused by the mountain.

chapters.title: The Valley of Names
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. On the eastern slopes they reach villages where Vessian descent runs thick and unrecorded; Sefa begins delivering the register door to door, families finding names they thought were lost. The beat is the archive dissolving into the people it describes.

chapters.title: What Vane Takes Home
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. At the trailhead, Vane accepts defeat with unsettling grace, taking only a single blank folio page as a 'receipt,' and warns that the Compact never stops buying. Ivo tells him the ledger will find them slower now. The beat is victory without triumph, war postponed.

chapters.title: First Snow
chapters.summary: POV Sefa. The snows close the pass behind them with a sound like a door; Sefa stands at the tree line watching the mountain seal itself over the chapel, the tunnel, the astrolabe. The beat is burial understood as preservation.

chapters.title: A Boat Called Kestrel Again
chapters.summary: POV Ivo. Downstream, the lockmaster's daughter returns the rebuilt kestrel-boat; Ivo repaints the name in full view, first time signing their real surname on anything in twenty years. The beat is stopping chosen freely — the captain who kept moving finally moored.

chapters.title: The Monsoon Chart
chapters.summary: POV both, alternating. One year later, monsoon rains swell the Serein; Ivo and Sefa run a schoolboat upriver teaching Vessian songs and river-craft to anyone aboard, the chest's contents copied and scattered beyond any buyer's reach. Closing the circle with chapter one's sandbar, now marked on their own chart. The beat is belonging as a practice, not a place.
